newsitem.title: USA: Fla. plans to issue 'LUST bonds' for leaky tanks.
newsitem.headline: Fla. plans to issue 'LUST bonds' for leaky tanks.

text.p: Florida's Inland Protection Finance Corp will seek state authorization Nov 19 to issue the state's first tax-exempt bonds to finance clean up around leaking undground petroleum tanks, corporation Treasurer Peter Collins said Thursday.
Because the program is known as the Leaking Underground Storage Tank program, state officicals have nicknamed the bonds "LUST bonds."

The size of the issue has not been determined but the legislature has pledged to allocate $65 million a year for six years toward debt service, with the restriction that interest and issuance costs cannot exceed $50 million, Collins told the Bond Buyer Florida Public Finance Conference here.
Issue size will not be determined until after the Dec 31 deadline for submitting cleanup payment claims to the state Department of Environmental Protection, or DEP.
"We think it's going to be pretty big," Collins said.
Already, there is a backlog of $348 million unpaid claims, and the figure has been growing by $8 million to $10 million a month.

The bond issue is an outgrowth of a cleanup program begun four years ago when the legislature authorized the DEP to reimburse property owners for the cost of removing old underground petroleum storage tanks and cleaning up the surrounding soil to prevent contamination of the aquifer.

The legislature established a $160 million trust fund for the projects but has already paid out $800 million in reimbursements. The program was halted two years ago becasue, "The claims were just coming in faster than they could pay them," Collins said.

When the program ended, some 4,000 sites remain contaminated, Collins said. The Inland Protection Finance Corporation was established to issue debt to repay claims outstanding claims, which are to be funded with excise taxes on petroleum sales.
The corporation will take its bond authorization request before the State Board of Administration, made up of the governor, comptroller and treasurer, on Nov 19.
"We don't expect any problem getting that approval," Collins said.

As a new issuer, the corporation will also have to seek bond valdiation at the circuit court and state supreme court level, which is expected to take four to six months, Collins said. Once that is done, the sale date can be set.
